req.title: Basic-auth handles special characters
req.statement: The system shall URL-decode <user> and <passwd> path segments before comparing against the supplied Basic credentials.

doc.reasoning: The requirement states that /basic-auth/<user>/<passwd> must URL-decode path segments before comparing against Basic credentials. I need to test: (1) positive case with URL-encoded special chars in path that match decoded credentials, (2) negative case where credentials don't match the URL-decoded path values, (3) boundary case with minimally encoded chars (e.g., space as %20), (4) decision-table case covering both user and passwd mismatch independently, (5) negative path with wrong password but correct user. The check_basic_auth function compares auth.username == user and auth.password == passwd, so mutations on == operators, boolean 'and', and the URL-decoding step are all targets.

tests.name: test_basic_auth_url_encoded_special_chars_positive
preconditions: httpbin Flask app is importable in-process
Path contains URL-encoded special characters (%40 for @, %21 for !)
actions: Send GET /basic-auth/user%40example/p%40ss%21 with Basic credentials user=user@example, passwd=p@ss!
expected: JSON body contains authenticated=true and user=user@example
tests.executable:
import base64
from httpbin.core import app

client = app.test_client()

credentials = base64.b64encode(b'user@example:p@ss!').decode('ascii')
headers = {'Authorization': f'Basic {credentials}'}

def test_basic_auth_url_encoded_special_chars_positive():
    r = client.get('/basic-auth/user%40example/p%40ss%21', headers=headers)
    assert r.status_code == 200
    data = r.get_json()
    assert data['authenticated'] == True
    assert data['user'] == 'user@example'
